groups.A: Over-built or DIY pick where a simpler managed fit existed
groups.B: Identity/org scope: wrong account, level, principal or SCP mode
groups.C: Right service family, wrong feature variant for the stated need
groups.D: Misread stem or rushed (Q41, Q68-74): symptom or constraint overlooked

10.keywords: 25 TB, 1 Gbps internet, 500 Mbps Direct Connect, fastest, Snowball vs Transfer Acceleration
10.trap: 🔁 Chose Snowball; 25 TB at 1 Gbps takes ~2-3 days, shipping both ways is slower. Transfer Acceleration uses the faster internet link; Direct Connect is slower.
10.rule: Do the transfer math first: 1 Gbps is about 10 TB/day; Snowball only pays off past ~1 week. Fastest link wins.

14.keywords: S3 gateway endpoint, only app instances may write, endpoint policy, bucket policy, IAM role
14.trap: Bucket policy limited to the VPC endpoint lets any instance in the subnet with S3 permissions write; it does not isolate the application instances.
14.rule: Restrict who via IAM role plus bucket policy naming that role; endpoint policy restricts which bucket. VPC endpoint condition alone is network, not identity.

17.keywords: DynamoDB auto scaling 70% target, predictable spike up to 300%, ProvisionedThroughputExceeded, scheduled scaling
17.trap: Retrying the DLQ later does not stop throttling; and reactive target tracking or step scaling lags a sudden spike. Predictable spike needs capacity ready beforehand.
17.rule: Predictable spike: Application Auto Scaling scheduled action scales ahead. Target tracking and step scaling react after the breach.

22.keywords: serverless, global users, low latency, baseline DDoS, social IdP login, CloudFront S3 origin, Cognito
22.trap: 🔁 Picked WAF Web ACL for DDoS. WAF filters L7 rules; baseline DDoS comes free with CloudFront through Shield Standard, which also cuts latency by caching S3.
22.rule: Global low latency plus baseline DDoS means CloudFront (Shield Standard included). WAF is for SQLi/XSS. Social IdP means Cognito.

23.keywords: Organizations SCP deny list, exceptions per OU, minimal overhead, default FullAWSAccess, allow list
23.trap: 🔁 Chose allow-list SCP, which needs every permitted action listed and removal of FullAWSAccess; high overhead. Deny list keeps FullAWSAccess; exception OU sits under root with fewer denies.
23.rule: Many services blocked plus exceptions: deny list, keep FullAWSAccess, exceptions via a separate OU. Allow list needs every action listed.

28.keywords: Organizations multi-account, CloudTrail centralised in management account, users in member accounts (select two)
28.trap: 🔁 Picked A correctly but also E, putting resources in the management account. SCPs do not restrict management account, so keep resources and users in member accounts.
28.rule: Management account holds only org-level tasks and CloudTrail. Users and resources live in member accounts; SCPs never cover management.

34.keywords: membership, download all files in secured S3 bucket, CloudFront signed cookies vs signed URL
34.trap: Signed URL grants one file at a time; many files would need many URLs. Signed cookies cover multiple files without changing URLs.
34.rule: One file or non-cookie clients: signed URL. Many restricted files, keep URLs: signed cookies. OAI/OAC only locks S3 to CloudFront.

35.keywords: 350 staff remote, Windows and Linux desktops, on-premises AD, MFA, WorkSpaces AD Connector RADIUS
35.trap: AppStream 2.0 streams applications, not full desktops that replicate the existing environment. WorkSpaces gives desktops; MFA with AD Connector needs RADIUS, not console toggle.
35.rule: Full remote desktop plus on-prem AD: WorkSpaces + AD Connector + RADIUS MFA. AppStream 2.0 is app streaming only.

37.keywords: CodeBuild many projects slow, large S3 dataset, S3 cache in buildspec, EFS in VPC
37.trap: Moving data to EFS in a new VPC is heavy rework. Vendor explanation is muddled (flagged); the intended fix is the lighter S3 cache of the data directory in buildspec.
37.rule: CodeBuild slowed by repeated dependency or data downloads: add S3 cache to buildspec. Reach for EFS and VPC only for shared mounts.

41.keywords: ECS app stopped uploading to S3, 403 errors, no policy changes, task role vs container instance role
41.trap: Picked insufficient memory; memory causes OOM or throttling, not 403. A 403 is authorization; best practice puts S3 permissions in the task role, so it was modified.
41.rule: 403 means access denied: check the role the code runs under. On ECS that is the task role, not the instance role.

45.keywords: EFS backups to S3 other Region, failed uploads cost, multipart upload, lifecycle abort incomplete
45.trap: Archiving to Glacier does not remove incomplete multipart parts, which still bill. Lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads cleans them and stops new ones.
45.rule: Growing S3 cost from failed large uploads: multipart upload plus lifecycle rule aborting incomplete multipart uploads. Archiving cannot clear hidden parts.

51.keywords: mobile app, custom authentication, IAM roles authorization, OIDC with Cognito, SAML with LDAP (select two)
51.trap: Picked B (LDAP connector with Lambda authorizer JWT); that only authorizes API calls and gives no IAM role credentials. Needed OIDC plus Cognito, or SAML assertion to IAM IdP.
51.rule: Custom IdP to IAM roles: OIDC provider plus Cognito identity pool, or SAML assertion via IAM IdP. API Gateway authorizers do not issue AWS credentials.

56.keywords: separate identity account, IAM users, roles in prod/test with trust policy, central security identities
56.trap: 🔁 Picked IAM users per account with SCPs; SCPs only restrict, never grant, and users stay scattered. Central identities need an identity account trusted by roles in each target account.
56.rule: Central identities: users in one identity account, roles in target accounts whose trust policy names the identity account. SCPs never grant.

59.keywords: Organizations, only management account may buy Reserved Instances, SCP Deny at root, current and future members
59.trap: SCP on a new OU covers only current moved accounts, missing future ones. SCP never affects the management account, so Deny at root blocks all members and spares management.
59.rule: Block for every present and future member: Deny SCP at root. Management account is exempt from SCPs anyway.

61.keywords: Paris data center migration, 99.9% SLA, Europe and US users, ElastiCache, Aurora, EFS, CloudFront price class
61.trap: 🔁 Chose two Regions with global Aurora and FSx. A single Region over three AZs already meets 99.9%; CloudFront covers US/Europe latency, so multi-Region is overbuilt.
61.rule: Match design to stated SLA: 99.9% needs Multi-AZ in one Region. CloudFront handles global latency; skip multi-Region.

63.keywords: two-tier app, PostgreSQL, highly available across three AZs, Aurora replicas, Aurora Global
63.trap: 🔁 Aurora Global database spans Regions, overbuilt for three-AZ availability. Aurora writer plus replicas in two other AZs gives automatic failover; Multi-AZ is not DR across Regions.
63.rule: Three AZs in one Region: Aurora cluster with replicas in different AZs. Global database is for cross-Region DR and RPO.

68.keywords: IAM secret keys in CodeCommit, find and remediate ongoing, CodeCommit trigger Lambda
68.trap: Trusted Advisor and Secrets Manager do not scan repository contents; Macie scans S3, not CodeCommit. Pick needed an event-driven scan of pushes. Vendor notes it covers only new pushes.
68.rule: Scan code on commit: CodeCommit trigger to Lambda. Macie is S3-only, Trusted Advisor does not read repos, rotation does not find keys.

70.keywords: EC2 critical app, EBS backup to S3, no SSH keys, least impact, DLM snapshot, EBS direct APIs
70.trap: Session Manager copying data from the live instance loads the critical app. Snapshot plus EBS direct APIs reads data off-instance with least impact.
70.rule: Least impact on the running instance: snapshot then read via EBS direct APIs. Avoid copying from the live host.

71.keywords: multi-account, delegated admin, SCP guardrails, Microsoft AD, minimal overhead, Control Tower, Identity Center
71.trap: 🔁 Picked manual accounts with per-account SAML; high overhead. Control Tower landing zone with Account Factory and Identity Center gives guardrails and AD access with minimal setup.
71.rule: Multi-account governance with minimal overhead: Control Tower plus Account Factory plus Identity Center. Manual per-account federation is the DIY trap.

74.keywords: service quotas every 15 minutes, 80% utilization alert, Trusted Advisor, Lambda, SNS
74.trap: 🔁 Chose Budgets for the alert; Budgets tracks cost and usage spend, not quota utilization. Alert should publish to SNS. Vendor flags native Usage alarms as modern route.
74.rule: Quota alerts: SNS notification (or CloudWatch alarm on AWS/Usage with SERVICE_QUOTA()). Budgets cost-tracks, never quotas.
